decisions.reason: As a consumer superfood drink it is weakly related to the firm's core waste-to-energy and industrial engineering knowledge, so management is likely to redeploy resources toward areas where its absorptive capacity and commercialization capabilities are much stronger.
Modular waste-to-energy plant extensions build directly on the firm's existing technical, automation and customer knowledge, making early market feedback easier to absorb and improve upon.

A waste-oil-to-energy plant is highly aligned with the firm's established biomass and waste conversion capabilities and is presented as a strategic flagship, so management would be inclined to continue developing it.

Although plastic-to-fuel is technically and commercially demanding, it fits the firm's core sustainable conversion platform and flagship direction well enough that management would likely keep it on the market while learning from initial results.
